originalTitle: BMW is taking on Tesla’s FSD with urban driver assist starting in 2027
summary: BMW says that it will expand its navigation-guided, partially automated driving capabilities into urban environments starting in 2027, launching first in Germany with other markets to follow. content: BMW says that it will expand its navigation-guided, partially automated driving capabilities into urban environments starting in 2027, launching first in Germany with other markets to follow. The new system can help steer, speed up, and slow down the vehicle on both highways and city streets using its built-in GPS navigation. While driving in town, it can assist with changing lanes, making turns, yielding to other cars, and driving through roundabouts. But as a Level 2 driver assist system, it still requires drivers to keep their eyes on the road and stay ready to take over at any moment. On the highway, BMW will allow drivers to remove their hands from the steering wheel — but on local roads, they’ll need to keep their hands on the wheel. BMW is the latest automaker to commit to releasing a partially autonomous city driving feature to its customers, as the industry races to keep up with Tesla and its Full Self-Driving (FSD) system. BMW, in particular, recently introduced its next-generation Neue Klasse platform, which includes a driver assist system partly powered by Qualcomm’s technology. And with hands-free highway driving now widely available in many mass-market vehicles, the next frontier is a safe and capable city driving feature that rivals FSD. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/DI26_000461417.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/DI26_000461418.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/DI26_000461420.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/DI26_000461423.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/DI26_000461424.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/DI26_000461426.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] BMW says its system works cooperatively with drivers rather than fighting their control, which means they can steer, brake, or speed up at any point to adjust their driving without shutting the system off. At the same time, the car shows what it sees and what the assistance system is doing right in your line of sight through the heads-up display and in a clear 3D map on the main dashboard screen. The necessary cameras and sensors already come built into models like BMW’s 3 Series, 7 Series, X5, iX3, and iX4. BMW can activate the feature through an over-the-air software update. The system follows new European safety rules that let cars suggest and make automated driving moves on city streets for the first time. BMW says that outside experts have already road-tested the setup and confirmed it meets the technical standards, with final official government approval expected in early 2027. With more cars equipped with partial automation hitting the road, safety researchers are growing increasingly worried about driver attention and the potential for these systems to cause crashes. There is compelling evidence that, regardless of the company, most driver-assist systems are less safe than normal human driving. Drivers tend to develop an overreliance on these systems to drive the car for them — even after a short period of use. And when it’s time to take back control of the vehicle, their reaction times are slower than what’s considered safe. BMW is entering risky territory with the adoption of a Level 2 driving feature. Much like Tesla, the company is emphasizing that drivers remain responsible for the vehicle even while using the partially autonomous system in urban environments. Tesla does the same for its FSD feature, but some customers have successfully argued in court that the company bears some responsibility for crashes when they occur.
chineseTitle: 宝马将于 2027 年开始推出城市驾驶辅助系统，挑战特斯拉的 FSD
chineseSummary: 宝马表示，将从 2027 年开始将其导航引导、部分自动驾驶功能扩展到城市环境，首先在德国推出，随后在其他市场推出。新系统可以利用其内置的 GPS 导航帮助车辆在高速公路和城市街道上转向、加速和减速。在城里开车时，[…]
chineseContent: 宝马表示，将从 2027 年开始将其导航引导、部分自动驾驶功能扩展到城市环境，首先在德国推出，随后在其他市场推出。新系统可以利用其内置的 GPS 导航帮助车辆在高速公路和城市街道上转向、加速和减速。在城里行驶时，它可以协助变道、转弯、给其他车辆让行以及通过环岛。但作为二级驾驶辅助系统，它仍然需要驾驶员时刻注视路面，做好随时接管的准备。在高速公路上，宝马将允许驾驶员将手从方向盘上移开，但在当地道路上，他们需要将手放在方向盘上。随着汽车行业竞相追赶特斯拉及其全自动驾驶（FSD）系统，宝马是最新一家承诺向客户发布部分自动城市驾驶功能的汽车制造商。尤其是宝马，最近推出了下一代 Neue Klasse 平台，其中包括部分由高通技术提供支持的驾驶员辅助系统。随着免提高速公路驾驶现已在许多大众市场车辆中广泛使用，下一个前沿领域是与 FSD 相媲美的安全且强大的城市驾驶功能。 [图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/DI26_000461417.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [图片： https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/DI26_000461418.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [图片： https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/DI26_000461420.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [图片： https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/11/DI26_000461423.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] [图片：https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/2026/1
